hints: Focus on shifting the equilibrium to the right, toward more $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, and think about Le Chatelier's principle for temperature and pressure.
Notice the forward reaction is exothermic with $\Delta H = -57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and goes from 2 moles of gas to 1 mole of gas.
Put the two effects together by choosing the temperature that favours the exothermic direction and the pressure that favours the side with fewer gas moles.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target direction**

We want the greatest percentage of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. That means we want the equilibrium to lie as far right as possible.

$$2\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(\text{g})$$

**Apply temperature using enthalpy**

The forward reaction has $\Delta H = -57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so it is exothermic. Lowering temperature favours the exothermic direction to release more heat.

$$\text{low temperature favours forward, more } \text{N}_2\text{O}_4$$

**Apply pressure using moles of gas**

Count the gas moles. Left has 2 moles, right has 1 mole. Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce pressure.

$$\text{high pressure favours forward, more } \text{N}_2\text{O}_4$$

**Combine both conditions**

To maximise $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ we need both effects working together. That is low temperature plus high pressure.

options.A: High pressure is correct for favouring 1 mole over 2 moles, but high temperature is wrong. High temperature favours the endothermic backward reaction, so it decomposes $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ back to $\text{NO}_2$.
options.B: High pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles, which is $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Low temperature shifts equilibrium in the exothermic forward direction, which also makes $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Both conditions work together to give the maximum yield.
options.C: This is the opposite of what is needed. Low pressure favours the 2 moles of $\text{NO}_2$ and high temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction, so this gives the least $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.
options.D: Low temperature is correct for the exothermic forward reaction, but low pressure is wrong. Low pressure favours the side with more gas moles, which is $2\text{NO}_2$, so $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ is not maximised.
